newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close up on Finance One performance.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close up on Finance One performance.

text.p: Better than expected support for the shares of troubled finance company Finance One Plc helped lift the Thai market late on Friday, traders said.
The SET Index finished up 8.22 points, or 1.47 percent to 566.39. The SET 50 gained 0.85 points or 2.11 percent to 41.15. Turnover 4.0 billion baht.
"I think the market rose because Finance One performed better than most people had expected," said a trader at a broker affiliated to Thai Military Bank.

Finance One Plc, which had been tipped to return from a three-month suspension at around four baht, opened at six and closed at seven in massive volumes which saw 135 million shares of a total 414 million company shares change hands.

"Rumours were flying that one or more foreign firms were buying. To be the largest shareholder you only need to buy 30 million shares and people say that it could be a cheap way for the foreigners to take over," said a trader at Cathay Capital.
Brokers said investors were inspired by talk that two U.S. firms may be interested and that the central bank was prepared to absorb some of Finance One's poor assets prior to a buyout.
Four traders contacted by Reuters said they saw no evidence that a commercial bank support fund was active in the market.
Some hope of a technical rebound in stocks at the start of next week and some glimmers of encouragement from economic data presented on Thursday also boosted sentiment, analysts said.
Bank stocks gained 3.46 percent. Other finance stocks, encouraged by Finance One's performamce, fared well having been well-primed for a rebound by recent discounts, brokers said.
Krung Thai Bank Plc added 1.50 baht to 29.75, Bangkok Bank Plc put on five to 151 and Phatra Thanakit Plc gained three to 36.75.
